newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African oil association gets first black member.
newsitem.headline: S.African oil association gets first black member.

text.p: The South African Petroleum Industry Association has agreed to admit its first black-controlled member, Naledi Petroleum (Pty) Ltd.
Naledi was established on March 3 and is owned by a consortium of black empowerment groups while coal company Sasol, which is not a Sapia member, has a 22.5 percent stake in the group.
Naledi will also be the first new member to be admitted to the association since it was established in 1994 to represent the oil industry. It will be the association's seventh member.
The other members are Shell, BP, Caltex, Total, Engen and Zenex.
Sapia said in a statement on Monday that it wanted to encourage new emerging petroleum companies to become members and would amend its constitution to encourage them to do so.
"In particular, alternate bases of assessing membership fees, making it more affordable for smaller members, have been proposed," it said.

Naledi director Moses Moloele told Reuters that Naledi would open its first petrol station on June 1 and hoped eventually to move into the upstream oil business, although this would probably take between five and 10 years to realise.
"We will weight the opportunities as they come," he said.
